reason: Changing the base multiplier literal from 1 in resolvePulsedWidth alters the pulsed width, and this exported function has no unit test at all.
Turning * into / in (pulse_width_multiplier-1)*clamp(intensity,0,1) changes the multiplier for intermediate intensities, but resolvePulsedWidth is never tested.
resolveDemandWidth returning undefined instead of the pulsed width is observable, yet no test exercises resolveDemandWidth.
Flipping + to - in the 1+(...)*clamp multiplier changes the resolved width, and resolvePulsedWidth has no test coverage.
The mutated 1 is the upper clamp bound 1-EPSILON for t, but baseT=(index+1)/(count+1) with tiny jitter never approaches 1, so raising the bound to 2-EPSILON never clamps and t is unchanged.
The directLength<0.001 degenerate branch returning undefined is observable, but no test uses coincident endpoints to trigger it.

When count===0 the fall-through yields empty meanderPoints and buildSmoothGuidePath([start,end]) measures exactly directLength, producing the identical {meanderPoints:[], pathLengthPx:directLength} the guard returns.
Changing nx*magnitude to nx/magnitude shifts point x for diagonal edges, but every test uses a horizontal edge where nx=0 makes both zero.
Widening directLength<0.001 to <=0.001 changes the early-return outcome at directLength exactly 0.001, a value a boundary test could construct but the suite never does.
Reading points[index+1] instead of points[index-1] as prev changes the Chaikin-smoothed coordinates, but no test pins interior smoothed point values.
The default comfort01 of 1 vs 2 both make resolveThrottleWidth clamp max_width*throttle01 (throttle01>=1) down to max_width, so resolveNervousWidth returns the same value either way.
Changing seed%628 to seed%629 alters the emitted phase0 field for most seeds, but no test asserts phase0.

Forcing the interval guard to false makes resolveVeinsPreset always recompute the preset and update lastHeartbeatCheckMs instead of holding the active preset; the resolver is production-reachable via VeinsSystem yet untested.
Forcing the empty-rules guard to false makes it skip the default-preset early return and compute from rules; resolveVeinsPreset is called by VeinsSystem but has no test.
Turning || into && in setWorldBounds accepts bounds when only one dimension is below minWorldSize instead of rejecting, which is observable but untested for a single-small-dimension input.
Changing width<minWorldSize to <= flips acceptance when width equals minWorldSize exactly, a boundary no test pins.
Removing the neighbor.isStatic skip would include static neighbors in the cohesion center, but no test places a static neighbor in range so it survives.
count+=2 doubles the divisor so the cohesion center is halved, but the test only asserts force.x>0 and force.y>0 which both centers satisfy.
Changing len<EPSILON to <= flips normalize to zero when len equals EPSILON exactly, constructible via a 1e-6 away vector but never tested.
Turning a 0 into 1 in the early-return {x:0,y:0} makes the disabled-avoidance path return a nonzero vector, but no test sets avoidanceForce or lookAheadDistance to zero.
Changing lookAheadDistance<=0 to <=1 trips the early return for lookAhead in (0,1], observable with a small lookAhead the suite never uses.

Forcing the t1-in-range check to true assigns t=t1 even when t1 is outside [0,1], changing detection for obstacles whose intersection falls behind or beyond the feeler; all tests happen to have t1 in range.
Changing projectionHeadingY*lookAheadDistance to / shifts the feeler endY for diagonal headings, but every test uses a heading of (1,0) where projectionHeadingY=0 makes both zero.

At lookAheadDistance===0, narrowing <=0 to <0 lets execution proceed, but the zero-length feeler gives a<EPSILON in lineCircleIntersectionT so no obstacle is found and it returns {0,0}, identical to the guard.

Changing overlapThreshold*1.25 to /1.25 flips resolveAwayVector between the direct and feeler-end vector for distances in the affected band, changing force direction, but the closest-obstacle test only asserts force.y<0 which both satisfy.

Bypassing the discriminant<0 / non-finite guard lets sqrt produce NaN or Infinity, so t1 and t2 fail the [0,1] checks, t stays Infinity, and the function still returns null exactly as the guard would.
